title: Rational-algebraic simple overfield for a p-adic algebraic element
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, write $k=\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], and let $\Omega/k$ be an algebraic closure [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. For every $x\in\Omega$ there is $b\in\Omega$ algebraic over $\mathbf Q$ [def-weil-algebraic-element] such that $x\in k(b)$, where $k(b)\subseteq\Omega$ is the smallest subfield containing $k$ and $b$.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, first bullet, p. 3: arithmetic input to countability of finite extensions. Exact project source proof: WeilConjectures/NumberTheory/Padics/Extension.lean:76–127, PadicAlgCl.exists_isAlgebraic_mem_adjoin_simple (declaration at line 82), using rational approximation, continuity of roots, and Krasner. Arbitrary algebraic closure follows by the field isomorphism of def-weil-algebraic-closure.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-padic-minpoly-normed-separation] to the given $k=\mathbf Q_\ell$, $\Omega$ and $x$. Fix its extending norm, monic separable minimal polynomial $f$ of degree $n\geq1$, and positive $\delta$. Thus $k$ is complete, nonarchimedean and nontrivially normed, $\mathbf Q$ is dense in $k$, $f$ splits in $\Omega$, and $\delta\leq\|x-y\|$ for every other root $y$ of $f$.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, first bullet, p. 3; explicit argument from project Extension.lean:82–127.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dense-subfield-algebraic-root-approximation] with $D=\mathbf Q$, $K=k$, $L=\Omega$, the norm and $f,x$ of step 1, and $r=\delta$. Its density, algebraic-closedness, norm-extension and positive-degree hypotheses hold. It gives $b\in\Omega$ algebraic over $\mathbf Q$ and $\|x-b\|<\delta$; the rational algebra structure is the specified composite inclusion.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, first bullet, p. 3; explicit argument from project Extension.lean:82–127.

proof.text: For every root $y\ne x$ of $f$, combine the bounds to get $\|x-b\|<\delta\leq\|x-y\|$. The extension $\Omega/k$ is algebraic by [def-weil-algebraic-closure], so $b$ is algebraic over $k$ as required by [lem-sfb-complete-normed-krasner]. Its complete nontrivial nonarchimedean base, extending norm, separable minimal polynomial and splitting hypotheses are supplied by step 1. It yields $x\in k(b)$, which together with step 2 proves the statement.
